slides.notes: Welcome. We will write the pieces of an agent and then give another agent permission to edit some of them. The office is fictional. Model and tool executions later in the workshop are real.

slides.title: Your first morning at Pending, Inc.
slides.notes: Read the manager line dryly. The participant is the person arriving; the employee is the agent. This illustrative handbook is not the actual baseline prompt.

slides.title: The customer was charged twice.
slides.notes: Fictional dialogue illustrating the real public double-charge fixture. There are two captured 4900-cent payments on inv-1. It must refund pay-2 while preserving pay-1 and the other account. Do not describe this scene as a measured model failure.

slides.title: What would count as doing the job?
slides.notes: Invite the room to name a failure: partial refund, wrong invoice, duplicate retry, false success. These become concrete examples when writing the scorer.

slides.title: Your manager has one more request.
slides.notes: Use the manager question to motivate the second half. Fixed model, editable harness. The learner first freezes tested tool-loop code. The editor cannot change the trusted final scorer.

slides.title: Here is our workday.
slides.notes: This is the three-hour Pending schedule. Allow 15 minutes at the end for final comparison and discussion. Keep extra implementation detail in worked answers.
